_comment: The range each checked setting must fall in. A range is {min, max, integer}: inclusive bounds, either optional, and integer true for a whole number. A setting sits at the path it has in its own file, groups included. src/config-bounds.js refuses a Bot Settings save out of range; the files' own values are checked at startup. The help quotes ranges from here. Only the shipped copy is read: an override could widen a range.

timers._comment: Every setting that becomes a timer delay, from any file or .env, is checked by src/timer-bounds.js: a whole number of at least minimum (seconds, or milliseconds for a key ending in ms), at most the lesser of maxDefaultMultiple times its shipped default and maxHours, well inside the 24.8 days a timer can hold (past that, it fires at once). An entry under settings overrides the rule: the poll intervals have their own ranges, request pacing is at least 5 ms and cannot be turned off, and the outage pause takes 0 to mean off. The dashboard's poll: half a second at least, or each open tab would flood the server; a minute at most, or its figures go stale.

_approvalMultiple_comment: Too small defeats approving ahead; too large wastes nothing but looks alarming in an explorer.
_rebalanceGasDeferPct_comment: At 0.01 nearly every rebalance on a chain with costly gas would wait; at 100 one may cost the whole position before it waits.
_rpcAccess_comment: getLogsChunkSize: under 100 a routine scan takes tens of thousands of requests; 10000 is the strictest cap an endpoint is known to enforce. rpcFailoverRatePercentage: at 0 every endpoint is out of service the moment anything is reported, at 100 none ever is. rpcFailoverRateDurationMinutes: past an hour the window measures history, not health, and the decider keeps a per-second tally across it. Each rpcRetryOn429DelaysMs entry is checked alone. rpcMax429PenaltyMs and poolScanReuseMs take 0 to mean off. rpcFailoverStickyMs: under a minute snaps back before the failure rate can change; past two days the bot in effect never returns to its first endpoint. boundedReadAttemptsPerEndpoint: past ten, a Manage click waits minutes for an answer its dialog should give sooner.
_historyScan_comment: A lookback under a year misses ordinary history; past twenty years predates any pool on these chains. An event cache kept under an hour sends long scans back to the chain every few polls; past ten years it never expires.
_priceCache_comment: A price cache under a second saves nothing; past a day it hides real moves. Inside a rebalance or compound it is held to a minute at most, or it would defeat that scope's fresh prices.
_positionBalanced_comment: A band under a tenth of a point is almost never entered; past 25 points either side, 75/25 would count as balanced. A quiet period under a minute lets a wavering split alert nearly every poll; past a day, a position balancing twice in a day alerts once.
_rescanPricesRecentWindowDays_comment: No days would re-price nothing yet report success; ten years outlasts any pool.
_impermanentLossGuardPct_comment: 1 is the tightest meaningful guard; 100 in effect turns it off, since only a worthless position would trip it.
_rebalanceOutOfRangeThresholdPercent_com: May be fractional, as the dashboard has always accepted.
_rebalanceTimeoutMin_comment: 0 turns the out-of-range timeout off; past a day, a position left out of range is not being managed.
_slippage_comment: The per-token figures reach 20, enough for a lopsided pair's thin side, while refusing a typed 100. slippagePct is the default both start from.
_minRebalanceIntervalMin_comment: A week at most; longer cannot be told apart from not rebalancing.
_rebalanceRangeWidthPct_comment: 200 is the mathematical ceiling: a width W means W/2 percent either side of the price, so 200 is 100 percent either side; more gives the same degenerate range.
_swapChunks_comment: swapChunkCount: two is the fewest that splits at all.
_correctiveSwapMaxRounds_comment: One round at least, or the step never runs; ten at most, since each is a swap paid in gas and slippage, and a price unsettled after ten will not settle on the eleventh.
_initialDepositUsd_comment: A figure the operator types for money already spent, so only a negative value or one no wallet holds is wrong.
_priceOverride_comment: priceOverride0 and priceOverride1: a token price typed when auto-detection fails. Zero clears it; the ceiling is above any price a token has had.
_autoCompoundThresholdUsd_comment: Its floor is app-runtime.json → compound.minFeeUsd, the fees a compound needs to be worth its gas, not repeated here; the ceiling is above any position's holdings.
_tokenDecimals_comment: An ERC-20 token's decimals, read from the chain or typed as an override. 77 is the most for which one whole token (10 to that power) fits in a uint256.
_rpcUrlCount_comment: How many endpoints the rpc list may hold: one at least, to serve a request; ten at most, since the list is walked in order on every outage.
_uiSettings_comment: The dashboard settings in ui-defaults_non-layout_for-server-up-scenario.json. Its timers, copyFeedbackMs, heapLogIntervalMs and dashboardPollIntervalMs, follow the timer rule above, and its on/off settings have no range. reloadMaxWaitMs: a minute at least, so a slow scan is not cut short; two days at most. lastCheckJustNowSec: 0 never says just now; past a minute the tag would hide a stalled bot. autoCompoundSyncHoldMs: 0 turns the hold off; a minute is past any poll's answer. activityLogMaxEntries: ten at least; past ten thousand the log slows the page. privacyUsdAmountThreshold: the five digits its input holds.

ilGuardRetry._comment: A minute at least, so a typo cannot retry every poll; thirty days at most.

throttleDoubling._comment: All three are whole numbers. triggerCount: two at least, since one rebalance is no burst; twelve at most, the highest daily cap, since a count no day can reach would silently switch doubling off. Each multiple: one at least, since a trigger window under one Min Time Between Rebalances never holds two rebalances, and a quiet spell under the current wait clears doubling before its wait ends. 1440 at most: at the shortest Min Time Between Rebalances, one minute, that is a day, and doubling clears at midnight UTC anyway.

tx._swapBackoff_comment: A retry after the price moved under a rebalance: the first wait from a second to an hour, the longest from a second to a day, past which the position sits idle for no gain. midwayRetryLimit: at least one try, at most twenty.

retire._comment: A drained position's grace before it is retired: at least a minute, so an abort is on screen first; at most two days.

compound._comment: Automatic compounds' spacing: at least one poll and one second, so two cannot fire in one poll; at most a hundred polls and a day, past which auto-compounding is all but off.

dashboard._comment: Under one poll the dashboard may never show the change; a hundred is past any useful wait.
